subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should OpenClaw classify and mitigate plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` failures in cron-backed agent runs?
rationale: The same provider 500 text can be treated as a local transient `server_error`, a shared provider `overloaded` cooldown signal, or a cron-local outage/skip state; each choice changes fallback, auth-profile health, and operator notification semantics.

options.title: Use server_error, no shared cooldown
options.body: Classify the plain API internal-server shape as `server_error`, keep shared auth-profile health unpoisoned, and prove cron retry/failure-alert behavior without changing cooldown semantics.

options.title: Use overloaded cooldown
options.body: Treat this as provider overload so same-provider profiles cool down, accepting broader shared provider impact during 500 outages.

options.title: Add cron outage state
options.body: Keep provider classification conservative and add a cron-local outage or skip state with explicit retry and notification semantics.

recommendation.title: Use server_error, no shared cooldown
recommendation.body: Classify the plain API internal-server shape as `server_error`, keep shared auth-profile health unpoisoned, and prove cron retry/failure-alert behavior without changing cooldown semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame points to steipete on the central classifier and cron retry surfaces where the policy needs to be encoded.
